clue.text: Article twice found among smalls — that's sick!

indicators.note: found among means the second article is also placed within the word for underclothes
twice signals the article is put inside the underclothes word a first time, with a second copy to follow

parts.note: smalls is British slang for underclothes
the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone finds something twice in their underclothes drawer and exclaims in disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' gives two copies of THE, which go in separately: UNDER-THE-WEA-THE-R. 'Smalls' is British slang for underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for feeling unwell or poorly is a common synonym for being sick.

clue.text: A French chap will welcome universal balm

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the outer pieces hold the letter inside

parts.note: a gent is a chap
U is the British film certificate for universal

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is happy to receive a soothing cream for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: An ointment or salve, a soothing balm.

clue.text: Flag impoverished Democrat raised?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: impoverished means poor

explanation.surface: A political question: was the flag of a hard-up Democrat hoisted?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a noun but is the verb, to tire or sag.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to weaken or wilt, which is to sag downwards.

clue.text: Rehearse during break, showing control

indicators.note: during places the practising inside the break

parts.note: a rest is a break
to train is to practise or rehearse

explanation.surface: Practising even in the interval shows self-discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-restraint is holding oneself in check, a synonym for control.

clue.text: Beating under cover

explanation.surface: A thrashing given in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a thrashing and the state of being concealed.

clue.text: Exposed to attack with an uncertain outcome

definitions.meaning: a contest whose result anyone could win

explanation.surface: A battle description: vulnerable, and nobody can say who will win.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes both an undefended position and a contest still undecided.

clue.text: Shred a short volume

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a tome is a large book or volume

explanation.surface: Tear up a slim book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shred' looks like a verb but is the noun: a tiny particle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount or particle, as in not a shred of evidence.

clue.text: Speech in support of ambassador's high-level cover

indicators.note: in a down clue the speech sits below, supporting the ambassador

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title given to an ambassador
an address is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A speech backing an ambassador's top-level cover story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-level cover' sounds like secret service talk but means something worn on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worn on the head is literally a cover at the highest level of the body.

clue.text: Clergyman covering area is a source of power

indicators.note: the clergyman goes round, covering the area letter

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar with a large parish turns out to be a powerhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear plant's core generates energy, so it is a source of power.

clue.text: Complained, provoked by head of government

indicators.note: by means next to, so the leading letter is put beside the rest
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: roused means stirred up or provoked

explanation.surface: Someone grumbled after being stirred up by the head of government.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble is a synonym for complain, as grouches do.

clue.text: Oatmeal intermittently used by designer for such a picture

parts.note: Christian Dior, the French fashion designer

indicators.note: intermittently means taking letters at intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: A fashion designer uses oatmeal in a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-dimensional scene or model display, a kind of picture made by arrangement.

clue.text: Language exercises adopted by new senator

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in by the rearranged letters
new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercises

explanation.surface: A newly elected senator takes up language exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercises' looks like the verb but is the school subject; 'new' rearranges the senator's letters, and 'adopted by' sets the exercises inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: An invented international tongue created by Zamenhof, so it is a language.

clue.text: Make changes, having rejected link across Germany

indicators.note: across means the backwards link spans the letter for Germany
rejected means turned back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tie is a link or bond
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Diplomats revise plans after a link across Germany is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns TIE into EIT, which goes round D.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise text or film is to make changes to it.

clue.text: Light lunch at home following quarrel

indicators.note: the home piece follows the quarrel

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel
in means at home

explanation.surface: A light lunch at home after a domestic argument.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglo-Indian word for a midday snack or packed meal.

clue.text: Reckless kid has difficult year

parts.note: to kid is to fool
hard means difficult

explanation.surface: A careless child is going through a tough year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child but is the verb, to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash and daring without thought of risk, a synonym of reckless.

clue.text: Sort of apparel that makes people curse?

parts.note: men are people
to swear is to curse

explanation.surface: Clothing so uncomfortable it makes people swear.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing for males is a sort of apparel sold in its own department.

clue.text: Furore over fortune seeing one with a nasty smell

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the furore above the fortune

parts.note: a stink is a fuss or furore
a bomb is British slang for a fortune, as in cost a bomb

explanation.surface: An uproar over a fortune, and someone thinks it smells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cost a bomb' is British slang for costing a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A prank device that releases a foul odour is one thing with a nasty smell.

clue.text: Careless mates put up ruin

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: mates are pals
to dash, as hopes, is to ruin them

explanation.surface: Friends offer accommodation, then wreck the place carelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty and sloppy work is done in a careless manner.

clue.text: Jump in hunt for work-related conversation

indicators.note: in places the jump inside the hunt

parts.note: to stalk is to hunt
to hop is to jump

explanation.surface: A leap during a hunt, and the hunters talk business.
explanation.definitionFit: Chat about one's job among colleagues is work-related conversation.

clue.text: Hurried across area for driving, soaked

indicators.note: across means the hurrying word spans the golf area

parts.note: sped means hurried
on a golf course the tee is where you drive from

explanation.surface: A golfer rushed over the tee and got drenched.
explanation.definitionFit: Immersed in liquid, as tea leaves are, so thoroughly soaked.

clue.text: Puzzle understood after dance

indicators.note: the understood piece comes after the dance

parts.note: a jig is a lively dance
saw means understood, as in I saw what you meant

explanation.surface: A puzzle is understood after a little dance of triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture cut into interlocking pieces, a common type of puzzle.

clue.text: Know-all wife is, for example, regularly busy

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A know-it-all wife is, for instance, always busy.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec or know-all, someone who thinks they know everything.

clue.text: Rugby player with ear gouged out, as it should be

parts.note: a prop is a forward in rugby's front row

indicators.note: gouged out means hollowed, the inside removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A rugby forward has had an ear gouged, which is how the game goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct or fitting, done in the right and appropriate way.

clue.text: Repeat part of speech officially

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to restate part of an official speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverberation that sounds again, or to say again, so a repeat.

clue.text: Sections must include a short lament for fliers

indicators.note: the sections must include the other pieces within them

parts.note: parts are sections

indicators.note: short means the last letter is lost

parts.note: to keen is to wail or lament for the dead

explanation.surface: An instruction that every section of a piece contain a brief lament for birds.
explanation.walkthrough: To keen is an Irish word for wailing over the dead; 'short' drops its last letter, and 'must include' sets it with A inside the sections.
explanation.definitionFit: Small long-tailed parrots are birds, so they are fliers.

clue.text: Call to mind being fine during the previous day

indicators.note: during places the fine piece inside the previous day

parts.note: the eve is the day before
OK means fine

explanation.surface: Remembering a good day before the event.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon up or bring a memory or feeling to mind.

clue.text: Hat that's best on international

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the best piece above the international

parts.note: top means best

explanation.surface: A sports cap that is the best one for an international player.
explanation.definitionFit: A pith helmet worn in hot countries is a kind of hat.

clue.text: Framework for each goal converted

parts.note: per means for each

indicators.note: converted means changed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rugby or football framework where each goal is converted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' suggests rugby kicking, but it rearranges GOAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden arbour of posts and crossbeams for climbing plants is a framework.

clue.text: Extend argument for name to be inscribed in record

parts.note: a pro is an argument for, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: inscribed in means written inside the record

parts.note: a log is a written record

explanation.surface: Someone drags out an argument about writing a name in the register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extend argument' reads as a phrase, but the definition is just 'Extend'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen in duration is to extend.

clue.text: Offence of 'Time Bandits' is overcharging

definitions.meaning: bandits commit theft; done in the time of light, it is a theft in broad day
charging far too much, a blatant rip-off

explanation.surface: A film review: the crime in Time Bandits is charging too much.
explanation.walkthrough: Time Bandits is a Terry Gilliam film; here it just means robbers acting by day.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a blatant swindle is a literal crime in broad day.
